Meet Musicless

See it in action
Watch on YouTube

Set it up once. Watch as usual.

  1. 1

    Add it to your browser

    Install Musicless from the Chrome Web Store or Firefox Add-ons.

  2. 2

    Turn it on once

    Choose “Turn on Musicless” on the page that opens. Reload any YouTube tabs you already had open.

  3. 3

    Make yourself comfortable

    Watch videos, Shorts or live streams. Musicless gets to work automatically.

You’re always in control. Use the music-note button in the video to restore the original sound. Press it again to remove the music.

A few things to know

Will every bit of music disappear?

Not always. Some music can remain, especially quiet music behind speech, and voices can sound a little different. Musicless keeps speech and singing. Try it with the videos you watch.

Where does it work?

It works on YouTube videos, Shorts and live streams. On a computer, use Chrome, Firefox or another Chromium-based browser. Musicless works in Firefox, Brave Nightly and Vivaldi on Android.

Does it upload what I’m watching?

No. Music removal happens on your device. Musicless doesn’t upload or save your audio, and doesn’t collect your viewing history.

Why does the video pause at the start?

Musicless usually needs 1–2 seconds to prepare the sound on a typical laptop. Seeking can cause another short pause. Slower devices may need longer.

Can I choose which videos it works on?

Yes. Open Musicless from your browser’s extensions menu. Turn off “Remove music by default”. Then use the music-note button in any video you want to process.

Which files can I use?

MP3 and M4A files, up to 10 minutes and 100 MB. Apple Lossless, protected files, and video files aren’t supported. Your download keeps the input format.

Does my audio leave this device?

No. Your file is processed in your browser and is never uploaded. After you select a file and choose Remove music, the page downloads the tools it needs. It reuses the saved model when your browser allows it.

Will all the music disappear?

Some music can remain, and voices may sound a little different. Speech and singing are kept. Listen to the result and compare it with the original before downloading.

Why isn’t it available in my browser?

The tool checks your browser’s audio and WebAssembly capabilities and the selected file’s codec. If a required feature is unavailable, try an updated browser. Processing speed depends on your device.
